doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Family roots, South Side and early training
title: Musical role models and the $50 piano at home
summary: She saw Fats Waller and Earl Hines as a child; the family bought a piano for $50 before she began to play.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Who did you get to see play music as a child? Who were your musical role models?

I used to see Fats Waller and Earl Hines. And I used to hear him play at the Grand Terrace (sings). He would tingle the piano all night. Raymond Walters, he was a Tatum protégée. But everybody in Chicago could play I think.
Now, you had a piano in your home?
Was that before you started playing or as a result of your playing?
How about any neighbors or extended family members? Did anyone else close to home show you or take you under their wing as a young child?
